tasks.subject: [community-self-host-launcher] [P1] Publish an immutable Community image and signed release manifest
tasks.description:
Add a Community-specific release lane that builds `apps/community/Dockerfile` for the supported Linux architectures, publishes it under a dedicated GHCR image name, and attests the pushed digest. Generate a signed, machine-readable release manifest that maps one DorkOS version to the immutable multi-platform digest, configuration schema version, a SHA-256 compatibility fingerprint of the tagged SQL migration corpus, minimum supported `flyctl` version, minimum supported Neon CLI version, and the manifest format version. Keep the existing main DorkOS image lane intact. Follow the CI stewardship change protocol for workflow edits and record the intended SLO impact before changing `.github/workflows`.

Acceptance criteria:
- The workflow attaches a release manifest only after image publication, both attestations, and anonymous digest readback pass; mutable tags are metadata only and can never be selected for deployment.
- The manifest signature or GitHub artifact attestation is verified against the expected repository and workflow identity before any provider write.
- The image runs as the existing non-root Community user, includes no source credentials, and supports both declared Linux architectures.
- A manifest/image mismatch, missing attestation, unsupported architecture, migration-corpus drift, or incompatible schema/migration tuple fails closed before preflight reaches consent.
- Tests cover a valid manifest plus tampered digest, wrong repository identity, unknown format version, and incompatible configuration fixtures.
tasks.activeForm: Publishing the immutable Community release artifact

tasks.subject: [community-self-host-launcher] [P1] Add deploy command dispatch and verified release resolution
tasks.description:
Add `dorkos community deploy` to the CLI command dispatcher and implement release resolution under `packages/cli/src/commands/community-deploy/`. Resolve only the exact requested or current DorkOS version through its signed manifest, verify its provenance, select the target Fly Machine's supported Linux architecture independently of the operator's local macOS or Linux architecture, and expose only the immutable digest and declared compatibility fields to later steps. Provide an explicit `--dry-run` path that can resolve the release and continue through read-only planning without writing to a provider.

Acceptance criteria:
- `dorkos community deploy --help` documents guided setup, dry run, resume, and the absence of automatic cleanup.
- The command refuses tags, bare image names, unverifiable manifests, unsupported CLI versions, and release/configuration incompatibility. A missing or not-ready exact-version manifest returns `COMMUNITY_RELEASE_NOT_READY` before consent, with no prior-version or mutable-tag fallback.
- A macOS operator can resolve the Linux image required by the planned Fly Machine without requiring a Darwin container variant.
- Resolution tests use local fixtures, including an absent/not-ready exact version, and never contact or mutate a provider.
- The packaged CLI can locate its manifest contract without a repository checkout.
- Command output contains the DorkOS version and shortened digest but no provider credentials or secret-bearing URL.

tasks.subject: [community-self-host-launcher] [P1] Build read-only preflight, launch planning and consent
tasks.description:
Implement `preflight.ts` and `plan.ts` for local binary/version checks, local provider authentication, explicit Fly and Neon organization selection, role diagnostics, compatible nearby regions, generated resource names, app-name availability, and immutable `LaunchPlan` hashing. Perform authoritative billing, quota, and role checks only where a provider's read API exposes them; label unavailable checks as unknown rather than inferring readiness. Render the exact Fly app, one-Machine topology, Neon project/direct TLS connection, private Tigris bucket, release digest, regions, possible billing, journal path, retained-resource behavior, and every unknown precondition. Require the operator to type the generated app name before the first write; reject `--yes`, piped stdin, CI bypasses, and environment-variable bypasses.

Acceptance criteria:
- Dry run performs the same read-only checks and renders the same plan, then exits without provider writes.
- No organization, region, or personal account is silently selected; stable identifiers and human-readable names are both shown.
- Missing authentication, known insufficient role, unsupported binary version, or unavailable region stops before consent with the relevant official provider link.
- Billing and quota are shown as ready, blocked, or unknown based only on authoritative provider output; an unknown check remains visible and a create-time rejection after consent is classified safely without a blind retry.
- Plan hashes are stable for identical inputs and change for organization, region, resource name, release digest, or topology changes.
- Tests prove typed consent is required on an interactive terminal and cannot be bypassed by flags, redirected input, or environment variables.
tasks.activeForm: Building preflight, planning and explicit consent

tasks.subject: [community-self-host-launcher] [P1] Add the secure journal, subprocess boundary and secret sink
tasks.description:
Create the non-secret launch journal, bounded subprocess runner, redaction boundary, and in-memory secret handoff used by every provider step. Store journals atomically at `launches/community/<run-id>.json` beneath the resolved DorkOS data directory with mode `0600`, schema versioning, plan hash, pending creation intent, provenance or idempotency markers, provider-issued IDs, verified bindings, completed steps, last safe error, and timestamps. Treat stdout and stderr from credential-returning commands as secret material held only in a bounded sink. Pass secret documents over stdin, never `argv`, and strip terminal controls from non-secret diagnostics.

Acceptance criteria:
- Journal writes resist symlink replacement, partial writes, permissive umasks, concurrent writers, and schema downgrade.
- Tokens, passwords, direct database URLs, signing/setup secrets, object-store keys, provider error bodies, and raw credential command output never appear in argv, journal, stdout, stderr, telemetry, or thrown errors.
- The runner enforces deadlines, bounded capture, a minimal inherited environment, cancellation, and typed auth/authorization/billing/capacity/conflict/transient/invalid-response/uncertain errors.
- Unit tests inject recognizable canary secrets into every input and output channel and prove none crosses the boundary.
- Journal migration tests preserve recorded resource identities and refuse a newer unknown schema.
tasks.activeForm: Building the secure launch journal and process boundary

tasks.subject: [community-self-host-launcher] [P2] Build the provider contract harness and sanitized fixtures
tasks.description:
Define the typed provider boundary shared by the Fly, Neon, and Tigris wrappers. Check in sanitized fixtures captured from the pinned CLI versions and pinned minimal Fly GraphQL operations for every machine-readable command or request the launcher trusts, plus version/auth failures and malformed responses. Add a mutation harness that removes, renames, changes type, duplicates, and injects terminal controls into every trusted field. Raw fixtures from commands that can contain credentials must be synthesized or irreversibly sanitized before entering the repository.

Acceptance criteria:
- Contract tests enumerate every external command or API operation, expected exit or HTTP status, output format, trusted field, deadline, and error classification.
- Removing or changing any trusted field makes the wrapper reject the response rather than infer success from prose.
- No test parses human console text or relies on locale-sensitive output.
- A repository scan test rejects credential-shaped fixture values and secret-bearing URLs.
- The harness can run with fake executables and a minimal environment on macOS and Linux without provider authentication.
tasks.activeForm: Building provider contract fixtures and mutation tests

tasks.subject: [community-self-host-launcher] [P2] Implement the Fly app, secret, Machine and release wrapper
tasks.description:
Implement `fly.ts` with typed, fixture-tested calls for authentication and organization inventory, app inspection/creation, region and app-name checks, staged secret import over stdin, non-secret secret-version and digest readback, pinned-image deployment, release/Machine/address inventory, checks, and app-scoped provenance where Fly supports it. Pin the tested `flyctl` version range. Preserve exactly one Machine and `--ha=false`; never build or push source during launch.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every wrapper result includes the stable organization/app/release/Machine/address identity needed for later binding checks.
- Secret import cannot place values in argv or diagnostics, and success is confirmed from non-secret names and versions rather than echoed values.
- Deploy passes an immutable image digest, keeps one Machine, and exposes enough readback to prove the running digest and applied secret version.
- Same-name apps without provider-supported provenance enter an uncertain/manual state and are never adopted.
- Fixtures cover lost stdout after create, existing foreign app, staged-but-not-applied secrets, two Machines, wrong digest, wrong organization, transient status, and malformed JSON.
tasks.activeForm: Implementing the typed Fly provider wrapper

tasks.subject: [community-self-host-launcher] [P2] Implement the Neon project and direct TLS wrapper
tasks.description:
Implement `neon.ts` with typed, fixture-tested calls for local authentication, organization and region inventory, project creation, and exact project/branch/database/role/endpoint identity readback. Obtain the direct, non-pooled TLS connection URL only in the bounded sensitive sink and hold it in memory for Fly secret import. Pin the tested Neon CLI version range. Treat project names as labels rather than unique identity and never recover a project by name alone.

Acceptance criteria:
- Successful creation records exact organization, project, branch, database, role, endpoint, and region IDs while excluding the URL and credential value from the journal.
- The wrapper selects a direct endpoint and preserves provider-required TLS query settings.
- Duplicate project names, a lost create response, wrong organization/region, missing endpoint identity, and ambiguous inventory enter uncertain/manual reconciliation without another write.
- Fixtures prove that name equality is never accepted as creation provenance.
- Errors and telemetry contain neither the database password nor a secret-bearing URL.
tasks.activeForm: Implementing the typed Neon provider wrapper

tasks.subject: [community-self-host-launcher] [P2] Implement the private Tigris creation and binding wrapper
tasks.description:
Implement the private Tigris wrapper with minimal authenticated Fly GraphQL operations because pinned `flyctl` storage commands do not expose machine-readable output. Obtain the existing local Fly session token only into the bounded sensitive sink; never pass it through argv, environment, files, diagnostics, or telemetry. Before creation, query the Tigris provider terms state and require a separate explicit acceptance when needed. After consent and terms acceptance, create a private add-on bound to the verified Fly app and independently read back its provider-issued ID, name, provider, organization, app binding, and private option. Query only those required fields: never request password, environment, SSO link, raw provider error, or whole metadata. Confirm the two expected AWS secret names through structured Fly readback. Deterministic naming and attached secret names are evidence inputs, never proof that this run created the bucket.

Acceptance criteria:
- The wrapper checks provider terms and cannot create until an unaccepted agreement receives its own explicit interactive consent.
- The create mutation has no public option and rejects any readback that reports public access.
- Success records only the non-secret add-on/bucket identity, organization, provider, and verified app binding.
- Lost response, same-name collision, wrong app binding, incomplete secret-name set, and unverifiable creation provenance enter uncertain/manual reconciliation without adoption or repeat creation.
- Fixture mutation tests reject missing add-on ID, changed app or organization identity, wrong provider, public posture, and credential-bearing diagnostics.
- No Fly session token, Tigris credential value, or excluded GraphQL field reaches argv, environment, journal, output, logs, telemetry, or test snapshots.
tasks.activeForm: Implementing private Tigris creation and binding

tasks.subject: [community-self-host-launcher] [P3] Create and prove the Fly app and private bucket
tasks.description:
Implement the Fly/Tigris portion of `execute.ts` using the transition `journal intent -> inspect -> prove identity or create -> inspect exact identity and bindings -> journal completion`. Create the app in the selected organization, record its provider-issued identity, create the private bucket bound to that verified app, and record only non-secret bucket identity and bindings. Use provider idempotency or provenance only when readback can tie the exact resource to this run.

Acceptance criteria:
- A normal run reaches `fly_app_created` and `bucket_created` with organization, app, network, bucket, binding, and provenance evidence recorded.
- A crash before create, after provider success but before response, and after response but before journal completion resumes without duplicate writes when identity is provable.
- A same-organization name collision or unprovable lost response enters `uncertain` and prints read-only reconciliation steps.
- Cancellation stops only the current bounded subprocess, records the last confirmed state, and lists retained resources without deleting them.
- Tests prove the executor never adopts a foreign same-name resource and never repeats a blind create.
tasks.activeForm: Creating and proving the Fly app and private bucket

tasks.subject: [community-self-host-launcher] [P3] Create and prove the Neon database topology
tasks.description:
Implement the Neon portion of `execute.ts` using pre-journaled intent and exact provider identities. Create a separate project in the explicitly selected organization and nearby compatible region, record its project/branch/database/role/endpoint IDs, validate the direct TLS endpoint, and retain the credential-bearing URL only in memory until secret import. Do not create a management key or persist the database URL locally.

Acceptance criteria:
- A normal run reaches `neon_project_created` with all non-secret topology identities and region recorded.
- A crash before create, lost stdout, duplicate project name, same-organization collision, and response-before-journal interruption follow the proven-identity or uncertain/manual paths without blind recreation.
- Provider inventory by name alone can never complete the transition.
- Region and endpoint checks prove the chosen direct TLS endpoint matches the planned project and branch.
- Integration tests use fake provider executables and prove no URL or password reaches output, journal, telemetry, or error text.
tasks.activeForm: Creating and proving the Neon database topology

tasks.subject: [community-self-host-launcher] [P3] Import runtime secrets and deploy the pinned one-Machine release
tasks.description:
Generate independent 256-bit authentication, invitation, and setup secrets in memory; combine them with the direct Neon URL; and stream the document to `fly secrets import --stage` over stdin. Confirm expected Community and AWS secret names plus non-secret versions/digests. Render a temporary Fly config compatible with the signed manifest, deploy the immutable Community digest with `--ha=false`, and verify one Machine, the running digest, applied secret version, public address, checks, and `/health`.

Acceptance criteria:
- The transition reaches `secrets_staged`, `deployed`, and `healthy` only after provider readback proves each state.
- The Fly config uses the direct TLS database URL at runtime, Tigris object storage, a disposable Machine filesystem, and the release manifest's compatible migration command.
- A crash after secret import but before journaling inspects actual provider secret versions and never regenerates authentication or invitation secrets based only on journal age.
- Wrong digest, unapplied staged secret, multiple Machines, failed checks, migration failure, or bounded health timeout prevents `healthy`.
- Tests assert that all five credential values and three Community secrets stay out of argv, files, journal, logs, telemetry, snapshots, and thrown errors.
tasks.activeForm: Importing secrets and deploying the pinned Community image

tasks.subject: [community-self-host-launcher] [P3] Complete resume, cancellation and uncertain reconciliation
tasks.description:
Finish the state-machine control surface for listing incomplete journals, resuming a selected run, reauthenticating, rereading every recorded resource by provider-issued identity, rejecting plan drift, handling signals, and presenting retained resources. Automatic retries are limited to reads and provider-documented idempotent operations. A create whose ownership or binding cannot be proven enters a durable `uncertain` state with exact read-only inspect commands and provider-console links; it is neither adopted nor recreated.

Acceptance criteria:
- Resume rejects organization, region, name, plan hash, image, identity, topology, secret-version, or binding mismatches before another write.
- Integration tests interrupt every state boundary, including lost create stdout and import-before-journal, and prove one resource or an explicit uncertain stop.
- Cancellation and failures always state what exists, who owns it, whether it may incur charges, whether data may exist, and the exact resume command.
- No failure path deletes resources or offers an automatic cleanup command.
- A changed plan creates a new run rather than mutating the original journal.
tasks.activeForm: Completing safe resume and uncertain reconciliation

tasks.subject: [community-self-host-launcher] [P4] Add owner handoff and applied bootstrap-secret rotation
tasks.description:
Implement `verify.ts` for the standalone Community owner handoff. After one healthy Machine is proven, show the exact HTTPS origin, offer to open it, and copy the setup secret only after local confirmation with a best-effort clipboard clear and honest clipboard-manager warning. Detect owner claim without receiving the browser session. If the setup secret is lost before claim, stage a replacement and deploy it before handoff. After claim, stage a fresh bootstrap secret, apply it with `fly secrets deploy`, and verify the new secret version on the same one healthy Machine and pinned image. Authentication and invitation secrets remain unchanged.

Acceptance criteria:
- The launcher never creates the account, proxies the claim, receives a password/session, or places the setup secret in a URL.
- Replacement-secret tests cover an already running owner-pending Machine and prove the new secret is active before it is shown.
- Completion requires bootstrap to be no longer claimable plus operator confirmation of one post and one private attachment upload/download.
- Restart between import and journal completion inspects provider secret versions/releases/Machine state and never assumes the staged value is active.
- Rotation tests prove exactly one Machine, the same pinned digest, health, and unchanged authentication/invitation secret digests.
tasks.activeForm: Adding owner handoff and verified bootstrap rotation

tasks.subject: [community-self-host-launcher] [P4] Package the launcher and document guided and manual operations
tasks.description:
Add a packaged-CLI test that runs outside a repository checkout and exercises manifest resolution, dry run, fake-provider provisioning, resume, pinned config rendering, and owner-pending output. Update the Community Fly guide with guided setup first while retaining the executable manual path for recovery and audit. Document prerequisites, provider ownership, explicit billing consent, compatible regions, public TLS to Neon, private Tigris storage, journal/resume/cancel behavior, secret handling, owner claim, custom-domain follow-up, paired database/object backups, and local DorkOS pairing.

Acceptance criteria:
- The installed package needs no source checkout, Docker build context, or unpublished file to render and deploy the pinned image.
- Documentation calls the flow guided setup, names every provider sign-in and approval step, and never claims one-click deployment.
- The manual Fly recipe remains executable and uses the correct config-relative Dockerfile path only for source builds.
- Completion output distinguishes deployment health from rehearsed recovery and states that Tigris snapshots are a separate operator choice.
- User-facing prose passes the repository vocabulary and writing-for-humans gates.
tasks.activeForm: Packaging and documenting the guided launcher

tasks.subject: [community-self-host-launcher] [P4] Add the separately armed credentialed release gate
tasks.description:
Create an opt-in release gate that installs the packaged CLI, verifies the signed release manifest, and provisions throwaway Fly, Neon, and Tigris resources only in explicitly designated test organizations. Require a dedicated spend flag beside each required provider credential or authenticated profile; ordinary `pnpm test`, `pnpm verify`, pre-push, and CI tasks must never receive the flags or credentials. Exercise one induced interruption and resume, owner signup, one meaningful post, private attachment upload/download, bootstrap rotation, and explicit cleanup with resource inventory before and after.

Acceptance criteria:
- Without every explicit arm and designated organization, the gate exits before any provider write.
- The run records non-secret release digest, resource IDs, state transitions, health, meaningful behavior, interruption/resume result, and cleanup proof.
- Cleanup verifies exact journal identities before deletion and reports any retained resource rather than hiding failure.
- Logs and artifacts contain no provider token, database URL/password, object-store credential, Community secret, browser session, personal data, or attachment contents.
- A release cannot be described as guided-launch ready until this gate passes against the exact packaged version and immutable image digest.
tasks.activeForm: Adding the armed end-to-end release gate
